subject: Groundwork: On-prem Kubernetes inventory, node affinity, and disk retention strategy
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@thornridge.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ops@thornridge.ai
Date: 2027-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Kickoff: inventory + retention requirements for on-prem cluster

Hi Rishi / Laura,

Thanks for taking this on. We're preparing to onboard a production Private deployment and want to make sure we hand you a sensible starting inventory and the retention expectations from our side. High level: 3 racks at our Seattle colo, two availability zones within the site, mixed GPU and CPU nodes, and strict retention for training logs.

Questions we'd like you to confirm in a short checklist:
- Minimal node types we should provide (control/infra/gpu/worker)
- PV classes you recommend for model checkpoints vs ephemeral caches
- Network layout expectations (service CIDRs, NAT/egress, firewall rules)
- Retention tiers for logs/checkpoints (default retention windows) and encryption at rest requirements

I've attached a site inventory template (site-inventory-template.csv) with what we have today. Can you review and call out obvious gaps before our sync? We're aiming for a technical sync next week.

Attachments: [site-inventory-template.csv (csv) — small template]

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Infrastructure
Thornridge AI

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-11T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: inventory + retention requirements for on-prem cluster

Sanjay — thanks for the template and the clear ask. Quick read-through below and a proposed next step.

Short answers (we'll expand in the doc before the call):
- Node types: Control plane (3 x control VMs across racks for quorum), infra nodes (kube-proxy, ingress, logging, monitoring), GPU worker pools (mixed A100/T4), and general compute pools for inference.
- PV classes: dedicate fast NVMe-backed PV class for model checkpoints (encrypted), SSD-backed for caches, and HDD for long-term archives.
- Network: We expect a private service CIDR (10.100.0.0/16), a pod CIDR per cluster (e.g., 10.200.0.0/16), egress NAT for outbound, and explicit firewall rules for control plane access.
- Retention: baseline recommendation below — we'll confirm with your compliance team:
  - Hot: 30 days (local SSD/NVMe) for recent checkpoints and logs
  - Warm: 90 days (encrypted SSD) for model history
  - Cold: 365+ days (object store/archival) for long-term retention

Action: Neha / Priyom / Dev can you review the inventory fields in the attached csv and add any required cluster-level details (network gateways, on-call VLANs, telemetry endpoints) so we can finalize the preflight doc? I'll schedule a 60m engineering sync for next Tue (2027-04-19) with a pre-read.

Reference: private on-prem checklist — https://drive.redwood.com/privatedeploy/runbooks/onprem-checklist

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Adding technical detail from the networking/storage side — summarized so the sync can focus on gaps:

Network / Security (must-haves):
- Service CIDR and Pod CIDR separation (e.g., service 10.100.0.0/16, pod 10.200.0.0/16). No overlap with customer infra.
- Control-plane access: limit to management VLANs and jump hosts; control-plane API only via private LB in the VPC + client certs.
- Egress: single NAT gateway per AZ with egress IPs pre-registered for your IDS/IPS.
- DNS & split-horizon: internal cluster domains need to be resolvable inside the VPC; ensure DHCP/DNS leases map to VLAN plan.
- Firewall: allow ports 6443 (kube-apiserver) from management, 10250 (kubelet) for monitoring, and 30000-32767 for NodePort if you expose anything.

Node affinity & topology:
- Use distinct node pools for: control (no user workloads), infra (logging/ingress), gpu-worker (tainted:gpu=true), and general-worker.
- Affinity: prefer anti-affinity for critical replicas across racks; use topologySpreadConstraints for replicas of statefulsets.
- Local SSD: use for fast checkpointing (mount as RWX where necessary) but ensure K8s eviction thresholds are tuned to avoid premature deletion of large checkpoints.

Persistent storage guidance: see attached PV-class guidance. Key points:
- PV classes: 
  - pv-nvme-fast (iops/high throughput, encrypted, daily snapshot)
  - pv-ssd-default (balanced latency, weekly snapshot)
  - pv-archive (HDD-backed, object-store exported via NFS or gateway)
- Snapshot cadence and retention: snapshots for pv-nvme-fast every 24h, retain 7 snapshots (7 days); pv-ssd-default snapshot every 72h, retain 13; archive kept in object storage with lifecycle to cold tier at 90d.
- Encryption: all PV classes encrypted at rest with customer KMS (HSM recommended for keys).

Operational notes:
- Backups: model checkpoints should be periodically copied to an offsite object store; do not rely on local PV for >30 days unless archived.
- Monitoring: expose tokenized push endpoints for Prometheus; include disk pressure alerts at 75% capacity.

Attachment: [pv-class-guidance.pdf — 6 pages, storage class recommendations]

Neha Kapoor
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick capacity sketch based on the inventory Sanjay provided and Neha's guidance:

Assumptions from inventory: 3 racks, each rack has 1 management switch, 12 x 2U nodes per rack; mix of 4 x A100 (80GB) per rack and 8 x cpu-only nodes. 40TB raw local NVMe available across cluster.

Proposed node pools / sizing:
- control-plane: 3 x m6.large-equivalent (low CPU, high reliability) — not on GPUs
- infra: 3 x m6.xlarge-equivalent for logging/monitoring/ingress (replicated)
- gpu-worker-default: 6 x A100 nodes (2 per rack) — reserve 10% for OS and kube overhead
- cpu-worker-large: 12 x cpu nodes (distributed)

Storage carve (initial):
- nvme-fast pool: allocate 20TB for active checkpoints (shared across gpu-worker nodes via local PV + CSI); snapshot schedule daily, retain 7 days.
- ssd-default: 10TB for caches and warm artifacts, snapshot every 72h retain 13 snapshots.
- archive: 10TB to be exported and replicated to your object storage weekly.

Eviction & retention policy notes:
- Set kube eviction threshold at 85% for nodes with persistent workloads; configure PodDisruptionBudget for stateful workloads and use StatefulSets with proper anti-affinity.
- For large model uploads, prefer direct-to-object-store transfer with validation; do not stage >10TB on local PV unless temporary and monitored.

I'll join the sync; Rishi please confirm the calendar invite time. Also I linked the Jira ticket for preflight items: https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-412
